newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says countermeasures possible in US port row.
newsitem.headline: Japan says countermeasures possible in US port row.

text.p: Japan may take action if sanctions are imposed against Japanese ships in a bilateral row over Japanese port practices, Transport Minister Makoto Koga was quoted as saying on Tuesday.
A Transport Ministry spokesman said Koga made the statement at a news conference this morning.
Koga did not elaborate, the spokesman said.

The United States, angry at what it says are costly and discriminatory Japanese waterfront practices, on Monday reiterated its intention to impose a surcharge on Japanese ships each time they enter a U.S. port from abroad. The sanctions are go into effect from April 14.

"Absent the comprehensive solution we are seeking, the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission will impose fees of $100,000 per voyage on Japanese liners calling at U.S. ports," U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
Bilateral talks in Washington aimed at defusing the dispute will continue on Wednesday.

Japan has admitted that Japanese port practices are in need of reform but is seeking to have the sanctions scrapped or at least postponed, after an interim agreement was reached between industry bodies to work on a solution by the end of July.
